## Motivation

Adapted sports for disabled individuals are not new additions to the world of sports, but they are often pushed to the side. These athletes receive less media attention and less public support but have the same drive to succeed. Performing data analysis using data from these sports brings attention to their importance and can help find areas for improved support from outside individuals.

## The Paralympics

Following World War II, when the effects of war left many veterans and civilians disabled, the Olympic Committee decided to hold the Paralympics for athletes with disabilities. The sports in the Paralympics are usually very similar to those in the Olympics with key differences that make them accessible to more diverse bodies. For example, the winter Paralympics include sled hockey, for which athletes play while sitting on bladed sleds, rather than the standing on skates that most people are used to watching.

## Data

The dataset provided (2024 Paris Summer Paralympics Medal Summary) was scraped from Wikipedia (see references for link). 

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Tidying Process"}

This process was used to make the dataset
- **Copied and pasted the data set into Excel**
- **Removed rank variable**

:::


<details>
<summary><strong>Variable Descriptions</strong></summary>

2024 Paris Paralympic Medals (86 cases with 5 variables) data:

| Variable   | Description                        |
|------------|------------------------------------|
| NPC        | Country's place in Competition     |
| Gold       | Number of Gold Medals for Country  |
| Silver     | Number of Gold Medals for Country  |
| Bronze     | Number of Gold Medals for Country  |
| Total      | Total Number of Medals for Country |

                       
</details>

Download Paralympics Data: [Paralympics.csv](phoebechar/paralympics/data_repo_submission/Paralympics.csv)

## Questions Investigated
1. What can be discovered through a medal distribution?
2. What percent of countries earned fewer than 5 total medals?
3. Is the distribution of total medals left-skewed, right-skewed, or symmetric?
4. Can we visualize which countries had the same total number of medals but different medal types?
5. Are there any outliers in total medal count?
6. If countries were ranked by total medals instead of golds, how would the top 10 change?
